text: The cap row and the reference data of rwb-case, the case list of rwb-case, the exposure of rwb-source-data, the Debt sale package of rwb-decision and the capability area of rwb-access are consumed on their owners' published contracts and never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-case holds the parameters and reference data of E1-042 and E1-043, only rwb-case writes recovery_case, only rwb-source-data holds the ACE views, and rwb-decision governs the rule rows. TSD S6 T5.2 names the module interfaces without an operation name and the plan's C row for this slice is empty, so no operation name may be invented.
read: FSD S6 A2.16.2, A2.16.3.1 and A1.4; TSD S6 T5.2 and T-A.1; context pack ownership rows and connection-matrix row S6; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.4 and R5.5 DP-05
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-source-data, before wave 4 starts
impact: The story builds on Day 1 against five contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a recovery_case row, a parameter row or a v_ace_* view fails the boundary test

text: The cap is evaluated by this service's own evaluator inside the workflow activity against the package version in force, and the cap has no route rule of its own: R-DS-19 and R-DS-23 are the only rows that name it, so no DP-04 kit row is added to the metadata and the rule kit dependency is tracked instead.
why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the step must test the cap and FSD S6 A2.16.3.1 lists no route rule, while the architecture places rule evaluation inside the owning service's activity. Adding RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or RWB-P7-E1073-CON to the metadata would invent a plan value, and writing a cap rule would invent a business rule.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 and R5.4 class H; FSD S6 A2.16.3.1; TSD S6 T2 and T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; context pack Temporal and Drools slides 12 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the rule owner in rwb-decision, before the package is tagged for wave 4
impact: The package arrives on its read with its version recorded in each decision record, and the kit dependency is tracked rather than added to the metadata row

text: The policy cap is a parameter and reference-data row of P3 rwb-case by the default ruling of Template and Rules R3, read at its version with the four lists; the published figure the 54 percent cap of R-DS-19, R-DS-23 and FSD S6 A2.1 is copied as a value and never written in the build.
why: No source names the field, the row key, the version or the owner of the cap. The only rows that name it are R-DS-19 and R-DS-23, the only figure is 54 percent, and R3 gives parameters (E1-042) and reference data (E1-043) to rwb-case. Any other owner or any constant in the build would be an invented business value.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07; FSD S6 A2.1, A2.16.3.1 and BR-S6-016; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; TSD S6 T3.2

confirm: Business owner of the debt sale cap and the solution architect, before wave 4 starts
impact: The cap is read from its row at run time and a fixture carries the 54 percent figure; a grep of the build for 54 percent finds nothing, and the row and version are recorded with each verdict

text: The basis of the cap the denominator, the population grouping and the period are not published, so the step records the basis it used with the placeholder, the absent cap row carries no message id, and no denominator, grouping or period is invented.
why: FSD S6 A2.16 and A2.1 say only that the population is held inside the policy cap and that the headroom is reported, and no source states whether the cap is measured on outstanding, on selling price, by segment or by cycle. A guessed denominator would be a business value, and no message row covers an absent cap row.
read: FSD S6 A2.16.1, A2.16.2, A2.16.3.1 and Requirements served; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; TSD S6 T3.1; legacy RWB-E6-012 Validation and messages
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6012-APP sections 2, 4 steps 5 and 6, 5 X3, 8 BR6, 11 and 14
confirm: Business owner of the debt sale cap, before the first cycle runs in SIT
impact: The decision record holds the basis the run used and X3 records its reason without a message id; the readability of the headroom depends on the basis being published

text: The cap step is called by the lot build and the award steps of DebtSaleWorkflow on queue rwb-debtsale; it registers no Temporal Schedule, no event and no job, writes no case state, no lot status and no award, and returns the verdict that its caller applies.
why: FSD S6 A2.16.2 step 1 names a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer while A2.16.4.4 declares No background event, the context pack lists 0 jobs for S6, DP-10 is absent from the pattern set, and the moves of R-DS-19 and R-DS-23 belong to rwb-case on the award step's answer. Any of those as a new trigger or a written state would duplicate a sibling story or invent a schedule.
read: FSD S6 A2.16.2 and A2.16.4.4; TSD S6 T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-19 and R-DS-23; context pack jobs 0, Temporal and Drools slide 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 and DP-12
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6012-APP sections 2, 3, 4 steps 1 and 8, 8 BR4, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6 and 13

impact: The step runs only on a call and an absence test fails a build that adds a Schedule or a consumer; the case and the award stay with their owners

text: The cap position and the headroom have no column in the service's tables, so they are recorded in the local decision record with the cap row version, and no column, table or migration is added by this story.
why: TSD S6 T3.1 declares eleven lot columns and seven account columns and none carries a cap position or a headroom, the legacy Data table names only decision_log_entry and rule_row, and DP-15 is not in the pattern set of this key, so a new column would be an unplanned migration and an invented field.
read: TSD S6 T3.1, T3.2 and T3.3; legacy RWB-E6-012 Data; FSD S6 A2.16.2 step 3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15
confirm: Solution architect and the ACE DB owner, before the schema baseline is tagged
impact: The headroom is reconstructible from the decision record alone, and a reviewer who needs a queryable position waits for the field set to be published

text: The capability area and the right of each surface are declared per surface and checked through the service-template guard of rwb-access; DP-08 is not added to the pattern set of this key and no guard dependency row is added to the metadata.
why: TSD S6 T6.1 gives the module a right per role and T6.2 says every endpoint declares its capability area and right, but DP-08 is absent from the plan's pattern set and the H, C and X rows are fixed. The check must still exist, so it is stated as a service-template capability and recorded rather than silently omitted.
read: TSD S6 T6.1 and T6.2; legacy RWB-E6-012 Permission checks; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08; split plan patterns DP03 and DP19
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The refusal path is built and tested on the fake while the guard dependency stays tracked; the read of the headroom follows the right of SCR-26 Award

text: This step publishes no event and consumes none: LotAwarded (EV-23) and AccountsTransferred remain the award and transfer stories', the decision record reaches rwb.decision-record.v1 through the platform library and not through a producer of this story, and DP-09 is not added to the pattern set.
why: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives the service exactly two events and IN gives ProceedsMatched, none of which is a cap outcome; the outbox library is a platform object and DP-09 is absent from the plan's pattern set, so an event here would be an invented business value and a duplicated producer.
read: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT and IN; TSD S6 T5.3; context pack service rows (event EV-23); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-09 and DP-14

impact: No outbox row and no producer group at this step, and an absence test fails a build that adds one; the library row is tracked for the award and transfer stories
